record.original_question: Let f(n) be the maximum graph distance, under diagonal flips, between two triangulations of a fixed n-gon, where adjacent triangulations differ by replacing one diagonal of a quadrilateral by the other diagonal. Determine f(n), and in particular decide whether the upper bound f(n) ≤ 2n − 10 for n ≥ 8 is optimal.

evidence.quote: Consider triangulations of a fixed n-gon. ... Let f(n) be the maximum distance between two triangulations. It is easy to show f(n) ≤ 2n − 10 (for n ≥ 8), which is conjectured optimal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer n ≥ 4, consider all triangulations of a fixed convex n-gon (i.e., maximal sets of pairwise non-crossing diagonals). Define the flip graph T_n whose vertices are these triangulations, with an edge between two triangulations whenever they differ by exactly one diagonal: that is, one triangulation is obtained from the other by replacing the diagonal of some quadrilateral formed by two adjacent triangles with the other diagonal of that quadrilateral. Let f(n) denote the diameter of T_n, i.e., the maximum, over all pairs of triangulations T, T' of the n-gon, of the graph distance between T and T' in T_n.

Determine f(n) exactly. In particular, it is known that f(n) ≤ 2n − 10 for all n ≥ 8; decide whether this upper bound is tight, i.e., whether f(n) = 2n − 10 for all sufficiently large n.
artifact.status_search_result: Lionel Pournin (2014), in "The diameter of associahedra," proved by combinatorial arguments that the diameter of the flip graph of a convex n-gon is exactly 2n − 10 for all n ≥ 13, confirming the conjectured optimality of the bound. This settled the question originally posed by Sleator, Tarjan, and Thurston, who had earlier established the bound for sufficiently large n via hyperbolic geometry.

status_evidence.title: The diameter of associahedra (Pournin)
status_evidence.snippet: The diameter of the d-dimensional associahedron is 2d-4 when d>9; two maximally distant vertices are described as triangulations of a convex polygon, and their distance obtained using combinatorial arguments.
status_evidence.claim: Pournin proved f(n) = 2n − 10 for n ≥ 13, confirming optimality.

status_evidence.title: Flip distance - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The diameter of the flip graph of a convex n-gon is 2n-10 for n ≥ 13 (Pournin 2014).
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is resolved; bound 2n−10 is tight.
